slowdown.note: She signed the 23 September 2026 letter calling for a formal agreement with China that would slow down frontier AI development (signed letter, not her own statement).

pause.note: The letter she signed asks for an agreement with China that would "potentially enact a mutual pause" in frontier AI development; a pause that is only a possibility and depends on China joining is mixed under the rubric.

intl.note: She signed the letter urging President Trump to negotiate a formal agreement with China to slow, and potentially mutually pause, frontier AI development.

rsi.note: No statement found on banning self-improving AI. The letter mentions automation of AI research only as a reason progress may speed up, not as something to ban.

record: Signed a letter with 16 other Senate Democrats, led by Sen. Van Hollen, urging President Trump to negotiate an AI agreement with China, including a slowdown and a possible mutual pause in frontier AI development.
Spoke at the Senate Banking Committee hearing "AI and the American Dream: Promoting Innovation, Affordability, and American Dominance".
grade_reason: She signed the 23 September 2026 letter, which calls advanced AI a technology that poses an existential threat and a danger to humanity. All of the evidence for this grade is that one co-signed letter; her own remarks on AI found here are about opportunity, jobs and trust (level D).
notes: Exactly 6 web searches ran; none was refused. Pages opened and read directly: the Van Hollen press release (letter text), Alsobrooks's 11 June 2026 press release, and the Baltimore Sun article reposted on her site. The A grade rests only on the co-signed letter; no statement in her own words about catastrophic AI risk was found. Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act: no source found showing her as a co-sponsor; the congress.gov cosponsor page for S. 5493 could not be opened (blocked, HTTP 403), so this is unconfirmed rather than ruled out, and the bill number S. 5493 comes from a search result summary only. The Baltimore Sun article is dated 14 March 2026 and says the call took place 'on Friday', so the statement date is given as 2026-03-13 (inferred). The Sun also paraphrases her as saying new technology could be a game-changer for the state if used responsibly; not quoted. Search results mentioned her bill on AI-generated election disinformation and a report with Sen. Wyden on AI use in Medicare; these are outside the scope (not catastrophic risk) and were not opened. The letter quote at level B is followed, in a separate paragraph on the page, by 'We should take these warnings seriously.'
